output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise is almost entirely bags whose tags the airport scanners can't read. Their share of failed reads went from 1.5% to 11.8% for tags printed on the new Fennick stock from 1 September. Transfer tags and Pelion tags are unchanged. Pelion uses the same handler and crew pool and its rate stayed flat. Corvane bags that scan normally are still at about 3.8 per 1,000. The extra bags sent to the manual desk are the ones missing flights; 91% reach the lateral after it closes. In a natural test on 14–16 Oct, counters using old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1%. The printers and handler were the same. So the tag stock is the cause. I can't yet tell whether the stock is defective or just needs different printer heat settings; check the printer maker's guidance and test that. What to do next: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock now (about five weeks are in stores and the contract runs to 31 December), watch the rate and read failures, and hold off on the breach notice and on a defect claim against Fennick until the stock-versus-setting question is settled. Tessaly's inexperienced crews may add some risk, but the evidence doesn't show it driving this rise.
